q1.title: What is the capability being changed, and is the claimed duplication real?
q1.imperative: Read main_effect_margin_uncertainty() and _axis_means() in full. Establish precisely what logic is shared (present tense: what the module does), what differs, and whether a single helper can serve both without contorting either. Record the code evidence.
q1.finding: REAL. Shared logic = one pass over the (driver,class)->value grid accumulating a per-driver-ROW aggregate and a per-class-COLUMN aggregate of float(value), in grid-iteration order. _axis_means (replication.py:111-128) accumulates sums+counts into 4 dicts then divides; main_effect_margin_uncertainty (replication.py:425-429) accumulates full value LISTS into 2 dicts via setdefault. Same key unpacking, same float() coercion, same visit order. _axis_means additionally accumulates a grand total/count the margin fn does not need. A helper returning the two grouped value lists is a strict SUPERSET: sums=sum(vals), counts=len(vals). Third consumer per_driver_demean (:155) already calls _axis_means and discards grand+class_mean.

q3.title: Can a shared helper actually preserve byte-identical float output, or is 'byte-identical' aspirational?
q3.imperative: Floating-point accumulation is order-sensitive. Determine which restructurings preserve exact bit-for-bit results and which do not, and record the constraint the implementation must honour.
q3.finding: ACHIEVABLE but CONDITIONAL -- byte-identity is a real constraint, not a slogan. Float summation is order-sensitive, so bit-exactness holds iff: (a) each per-axis accumulation still visits cell values in grid-iteration order (setdefault-append in the same loop preserves it); (b) the GRAND mean stays its own single left-to-right accumulation over grid values -- re-deriving it by concatenating driver rows REORDERS the addition and can shift the last ulp, and math.fsum is a different algorithm entirely; (c) _main_effect_se (replication.py:397-405) feeds its list to np.std(ddof=1), so that list's order must be preserved too. sum(list_in_grid_order) is bit-identical to the current 'total = 0.0; total += v' loop (implicit int-0 start then 0+v0 == 0.0+v0). Dict key INSERTION order is preserved by setdefault-in-grid-order, keeping report/repr determinism.

q4.title: Which helper shape: grouped value lists, or sums+counts?
q4.imperative: _axis_means needs only per-axis sums and counts; main_effect_margin_uncertainty needs the full per-axis value lists (for a std). A single helper must pick one shape. This is a seam-placement choice the principal owns — take it to them, do not self-answer.
q4.finding: DECISION -- no human reachable; resolved under the engagement's standing instruction (record the question, decide it myself, carry on). ASKED: should the shared helper return grouped value LISTS, or per-axis sums+counts? DECIDED: grouped value lists -- _axis_groups(grid) -> (driver_rows: dict[object, list[float]], class_cols: dict[object, list[float]]), with _axis_means keeping its own separate single pass for the grand mean. Rationale: lists are the superset shape both callers can be served from (sum/len recovers what _axis_means needs), and the margin fn literally materialises exactly this today, so it becomes a pure deletion there. The sums+counts alternative FAILS the margin caller -- it needs the values themselves for a std and would have to re-walk the grid, deduplicating nothing. Cost: _axis_means transiently holds one float per cell instead of 4 scalar dicts -- negligible on a ~20-driver x few-class grid. @grade: settled/human (engagement standing instruction) -- revisitable by the owner at implementation.

consolidation.summary: #704 is a pure in-file structural dedup of replication.py with a CLOSED, fully-enumerated blast radius (nothing outside the module touches _axis_means).
